questions.stem: A doctor explains that a patient's stomach lining is damaged. At which level of organisation is the stomach lining?

options.text: Cell
Tissue
Organ
Organ system

questions.explanation: The stomach lining is a tissue -- a group of similar cells working together to perform a specific function (in this case, producing mucus and enzymes). The stomach itself is an organ (made of several tissues), while the entire digestive tract is an organ system.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly lists structures from the simplest to the most complex level of organisation?

options.text: Tissue, cell, organ, organ system, organism
Cell, organ, tissue, organ system, organism
Cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism
Organ system, organ, tissue, cell, organism

questions.explanation: The correct hierarchy from simplest to most complex is: cell (basic unit of life), tissue (group of similar cells), organ (group of different tissues), organ system (group of organs working together), organism (complete living thing).

questions.stem: The heart contains muscle tissue, nerve tissue, blood tissue, and connective tissue. This makes the heart an example of which level of organisation?

options.text: A tissue, because it performs one function
An organ, because it is made of different tissues working together
An organ system, because it contains multiple tissues
A cell, because it is a single structure

questions.explanation: An organ is defined as a structure made up of different types of tissues working together to perform a specific function. The heart contains muscle tissue (for pumping), nerve tissue (for controlling rhythm), blood tissue, and connective tissue, making it an organ within the circulatory system.

questions.stem: A leaf contains palisade mesophyll, spongy mesophyll, epidermal tissue, and xylem/phloem. A student says the leaf is a tissue. Why are they incorrect?

options.text: A leaf is actually a cell
A leaf contains only one type of tissue
A leaf is an organ because it contains multiple different tissues working together
A leaf is an organ system

questions.explanation: A tissue is a group of similar cells performing the same function. Since a leaf contains multiple different types of tissue (palisade mesophyll, spongy mesophyll, epidermal, and vascular tissues), it is classified as an organ. The organ system would be the entire shoot system of the plant.

questions.stem: Cancer involves cells dividing uncontrollably. If cancer starts in one tissue, it can spread to other organs. At which level of organisation does cancer initially begin?

options.text: Organism level
Organ system level
Cellular level
Organ level

questions.explanation: Cancer begins at the cellular level when a single cell undergoes mutations that cause it to divide uncontrollably. These abnormal cells then form a tumour (tissue level) and can eventually spread (metastasise) to other organs and organ systems. Understanding this helps explain why early detection at the cellular level is important.
